title: Dangermond Preserve — Creek Water Outlines
snippet: Outlines of where creek water would sit at a range of water surface elevations (WSE), for every short stretch of creek in the Jack and Laura Dangermond Preserve.
description:
What this is
Water outlines for the creeks of the Jack and Laura Dangermond Preserve, California. Each short stretch of creek has a set of outlines showing where water would sit at a range of water surface elevations (WSE), in meters above the North American Vertical Datum of 1988 (NAVD88). The steps are 5 centimeters apart up to the highest estimated level, then 25 centimeters apart for 2 meters above it. Pair them with the companion inferred creek water surface elevation layer to see where the water was at any hour.

How it was made
For each stretch and each water surface elevation, we filled the USGS 3D Elevation Program (3DEP) 1-meter bare-earth terrain with water, from the lowest point of the channel up to that height, and traced the edge of the wet area. Each outline extends 2 meters past the waterline so it tucks under the banks on a 3D map. On a 3D map, the surface slopes downstream between the estimated levels at each end of the stretch, so neighboring stretches meet smoothly.

Data used

  • USGS 3DEP 1-meter bare-earth terrain.
  • The Nature Conservancy creek centerlines.
  • Inferred water surface elevations from the companion layer, which combine modeled stream flow from the NOAA National Water Model and the California Natural Flows Database using Manning's equation (version m1-v1).

Accuracy and limits
These outlines carry every limit of the inferred water surface elevations they are built from. The terrain can't see below the water surface, so low-water outlines are approximate. The outlines are flat 2D shapes; a 3D map sets their height from the water surface elevation.

What's inside

  • One outline per creek stretch per water-height step, each listing the lowest and highest water surface elevation it covers.
  • A versions table. New versions are added next to the old ones, never replacing them.

Version m1-v1. Produced by the UCSB Spatial Center for the Dangermond Preserve Digital Twin.
accessInformation: USGS 3D Elevation Program; The Nature Conservancy; NOAA National Water Model v3.0 retrospective; California Natural Flows Database. Derived by the UCSB Spatial Center.
licenseInfo: Inferred estimates for research and visualization. Not measurements; see Accuracy and limits. Please credit the UCSB Spatial Center and the source datasets listed.
